analysis: The PR only changes docs/developer/test.md. It inserts a documentation section, 'Deadline Admission Estimators' (head lines 113-137), describing offline test suites: EngineMeasurementOrderingTests, AdmissionRateEstimatorTests, CBv2PerBatchDecodeChargeTests and CBv2PerBatchDecodeConversionTests. It also gives one swift test command and a note to run the SDK suites from libs/mlx-swift-lm/ with --filter CBv2PerBatchDecode. I checked the added text against the threat model (TB-002, TB-011 and the App Attest, authorization and cache threats). It touches no source code, authentication, attestation, encryption, key handling, authorization or data-exposure paths. It also does not change the trust boundaries, coordinator or provider behavior, workflows, secrets, or endpoints. The commands use scripted engines and synthetic numeric usage and need no model, GPU or production state. The text states that they do not qualify live refusal rates, hardware performance or routing, so it makes no new trust or qualification claim and does not weaken any mitigation. Base and head match outside the insertion apart from the shift in line numbers; the remainder of the file is unchanged. Limits: I did not see the test sources or the admission estimator code the section describes. Any security effect of the underlying deadline-admission or rate-estimator implementation, such as DoS or capacity gating, would belong to that code's own review. This documentation-only change creates no concrete regression and no gap that requires a threat-model update.
